content_map.problem: Agent applications often need explicit control flow, persisted state, failure recovery and human intervention around model/tool calls; a simple model loop does not provide those orchestration guarantees by itself.
content_map.thesis: LangGraph provides a low-level graph-oriented orchestration runtime where deterministic and agentic steps operate over explicit state, while checkpointers persist thread-scoped graph state for interruption, recovery and continuation.
sections: Boundary with higher-level agent frameworks and deployment tooling
mechanisms: A StateGraph defines explicit nodes and edges over application state so deterministic code and LLM-driven steps can coexist in one orchestration graph.
Checkpointers persist graph-state snapshots scoped to a thread, supporting continuity, interruption, time travel and fault recovery.
Stores persist application-defined data across threads and therefore solve a different persistence problem from thread checkpoints.
Human-in-the-loop capabilities operate by pausing around graph state so a person can inspect or modify state before execution continues.
examples: An agent graph routes between deterministic validation, an LLM planning node and a tool-execution node while keeping explicit shared state.
A long-running agent pauses for human approval, persists its thread state and later resumes instead of reconstructing the entire run from conversational text.
A workflow stores user preferences across threads in a Store while thread-specific execution state remains in checkpoints.
claims: LangGraph describes itself as a low-level orchestration framework/runtime for long-running, stateful agents.
LangGraph supports mixing deterministic hand-coded steps with LLM-driven agentic steps in one graph.
LangGraph persistence uses checkpointers for thread-scoped graph-state snapshots and Stores for longer-lived application-defined data across threads.
Persistence enables continuation after interruptions/failures and supports human-in-the-loop workflows.
evidence: Official LangGraph overview and persistence documentation inspected 2026-08-27.
assumptions: The agent application benefits from explicit orchestration rather than only a prebuilt model/tool loop.
Execution state must survive interruptions or be inspected across steps.
The application owner is willing to model state and control-flow boundaries explicitly.
limitations: LangGraph orchestration does not by itself provide authorization policy, protected-data boundaries or the broader governance semantics represented by the project's controlled-execution concept.

A graph/checkpoint runtime is not the same abstraction as the ReAct reasoning/action/observation method; a ReAct-style loop can be implemented inside an orchestration graph but they answer different questions.

LangGraph durable execution/persistence overlaps with Temporal at a reliability goal level, but the products expose different runtime models and should not be treated as interchangeable implementations.
Persistence still requires selecting and operating a suitable checkpointer/store; an in-memory saver does not survive process restart.
open_questions: Which agent workflows genuinely need low-level graph control rather than a higher-level agent abstraction?
Where should an application use LangGraph persistence versus an external workflow engine or system-of-record state?

selection.requested_focus: Understand LangGraph's model for resilient agent orchestration, state, control flow and durable execution; compare the responsibilities with the existing ReAct/Temporal/controlled-execution model without forcing equivalence.
coherent_core: LangGraph is primarily an orchestration runtime: explicit graph state and control flow around agent work.
Deterministic and agentic steps can be composed in one graph instead of forcing every transition through an LLM loop.
Checkpoints persist thread-scoped graph state while Stores retain application-defined data across threads.
This refines the project's controlled/durable execution knowledge but does not collapse into ReAct or Temporal.
prerequisites: difference between thread execution state and cross-thread memory
difference between orchestration runtime and agent reasoning strategy
drop_notes: LangSmith tracing/deployment features are adjacent ecosystem capabilities, not part of the minimal open-source LangGraph mental model.
API syntax and higher-level LangChain/Deep Agents abstractions are omitted from the central model.
Marketing adoption claims are not needed for the architectural insight.
connections: Controlled execution is refined only at the orchestration/persistence layer; policy and authority remain separate concerns.
Durable execution is reinforced/refined as a goal, but LangGraph checkpointed graph state and Temporal Workflow/Event History remain different runtime abstractions.
ReAct remains a reasoning/action strategy that may run inside a graph rather than an equivalent orchestration model.
